title: A common-field fibre of a pulled-back family surjects onto a prescribed field fibre
statement: Let f:X\to S and g:T\to S be arbitrary scheme morphisms and t in T, s in S with g(t)=s. Fix a field K and a morphism y:Spec K\to Spec kappa(s). There exist a field E in the same universe, a morphism z:Spec E\to Spec kappa(t), and a surjective morphism p:(X times_S T)_t times_{kappa(t)} Spec E\to X_s times_{kappa(s)} Spec K [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product]. There are no finite type or etaleness hypotheses and no subsets or covering families in this statement.

source.place: Tag 055G, transfer from the model to field fibres; Mathlib PullbackCarrier and pullback pasting.

proof.text: Choose the unique points of Spec kappa(t) and Spec K. They have equal image s in S. Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback gives a point r of the product of these field spectra over S. Its residue field E has compatible maps z to Spec kappa(t) and k to Spec K, by the pullback condition.

Apply pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso twice on each side and pullback.congrHom to the compatibility equation. This identifies the geometric fibre of the pulled-back family over t with the k-base change of the prescribed K-fibre. The map k between nonempty singleton field spectra is surjective. Its base-change first projection is surjective, as is the composite with the pullback isomorphism; this composite is p. All objects in the proof are constructed by pullbacks, residue fields, and canonical isomorphisms.
